title: GsOQDC: A GUI-Driven Interactive Framework for End-to-End Simulation of Optical Quantum Data Centers
authors: Seyed Navid Elyasi, Sima Bahrani, Rui Wang, Dimitra Simeonidou, Paolo Monti, Rui Lin
abstract: We present GsOQDC, an open-source graphical framework integrating optical-network design, distributed quantum-circuit compilation, scheduling, and DES-based remote-gate simulation, enabling end-to-end cross-layer evaluation of entanglement-resource dynamics and system-level performance in Optical Quantum Data Centers.
summary: The paper introduces GsOQDC, an open-source GUI framework designed to simulate Optical Quantum Data Centers (OQDCs) for Distributed Quantum Computation. It unifies the entire workflow—from circuit design through network scheduling and execution simulation—into one platform. This allows researchers to evaluate complex cross-layer performance metrics like entanglement dynamics and system fidelity in a practical, graphical environment.
main_problem: The existing software ecosystem for Quantum Data Centers (QDCs) is fragmented, lacking an integrated environment to evaluate end-to-end behavior across quantum applications and optical network resources.
main_result: GsOQDC provides the first graphical platform enabling end-to-end design-space exploration of distributed quantum applications while jointly considering optical-network behavior and entanglement-resource dynamics.
method: The framework integrates circuit modeling, optically switched interconnection, network-aware compilation, scheduling, and a Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) engine for cross-layer evaluation.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an Optical Quantum Data Center (OQDC), comprising multiple interconnected Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) linked by optical networks to perform Distributed Quantum Computation (DQC).
key_observables: Entanglement-resource dynamics, system-level performance, Fidelity, Communication overhead, Entanglement-resource utilization, and Job Execution Time (JET).
important_parameters: Gate errors, coherence times, network architecture parameters, and scheduling constraints.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the need to bridge gaps between tools that either lack compilation/scheduling or assume abstract communication models.

paper_structure: The paper introduces GsOQDC, detailing its architecture (Fig. 1), providing an interactive GUI for network design and parameter setting (Fig. 2), and demonstrating the simulation of complex workloads via scheduling visualizations (Fig. 3).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the practical engineering challenge of simulating large-scale quantum networking, which underpins future distributed quantum computation architectures.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: GsOQDC workflow and software architecture. The platform integrates the end-to-end DQC workflow, enabling users to progress from quantum-circuit design and optical-network configuration to distributed compilation, scheduling, execution, and performance evaluation within a single graphical environment.

Fig. 2: GsOQDC Network Designer. (a) Interactive topology editor for constructing Optical Quantum Data Center architectures using QPUs, optical components, and communication links. (b) Component configuration panel, accessible via right-click, allowing users to modify hardware and noise parameters, including qubit properties, gate errors, coherence times, readout errors, and device-specific calibration data. Together, these capabilities enable realistic, cross-layer modeling of distributed quantum-computing infrastructures.

Fig. 3: Distributed-workload scheduling in GsOQDC. (a) Interactive Gantt-chart visualization showing local operations, remote-gate execution, and communication events across multiple QPUs. (b) Contextual information panel displayed when hovering over a scheduled operation, providing timing, duration, resource, and process details. (c) User-configurable gate and process timing parameters.
